Ministry’s Reply
The Madras Port Trust Regulations, relating to Provident Fund and Gratuity framed under the erstwhile Madras Port Trust Act, 1905 continued to
be in force as ‘deemed Regulations’ under Section 133 (20) (c) of the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 which deal with both contributory Provident
Fund and General Provident fund.
The Pension Schemes were introduced in the Madras Port Trust with effect from 1
st April, 1963 and the grant of Pensionary benefits are regulated
under the provisions of the Madras Port Trust Pension Regulations, 1987, which have been framed in replacement of the then existing Pension
Rules, 1963.
Consequent on the introduction of the Pension Scheme effective from 1st April, 1963 all persons appointed on or after 1st April, 1963 are
compulsorily governed by the General Provident Fund Schemes.
As such, the Contributory Provident Fund Provisions as contained in the Provident Fund and Gratuity Regulations are applicable only to such of
those employees who have been admitted to the contributory provident Fund prior to the enforcement of the Pension Scheme. The contributory
Provident Fund Regulations will cease to be in operation with the retirement of the last contributory Provident Fund subscriber in the year 2003.
Further due to the re-classification of various categories of posts and bringing the category of Artisans and Labourers into one Schedule of
employees, in accordance with the provisions of Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 some of the provisions of the Provident Fund and Gratuity
Regulations have become obsolete.
While awarding approval to the Trust’s proposal for adoption of the orders contained in the Government Notification No. 20 (6)/Pen/P&PW/86
dated 8.2.1987 extending certain liberalisations with regard to nomination etc., under the contributory Provident Fund Rules, the Ministry in their
letter No. PR-12016/16/87-PEI, dated 14.1.1988 instructed that revised Regulations in supersession of the existing Regulations might be framed by
the Trust under the provisions of the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963.
In compliance with Government’s instruction two separate sets of Regulations viz. Madras Port Trust (General Provident Fund) Regulations and
Madras Port Trust (Contributory Provident Fund) Regulations were framed on the pattern of central Government Rules.
Committee’s observation
The Committee noted the reply of the Ministry and observed that there was some delay in framing of these regulations, after instructions from the
Government that revised regulations might be framed under the provision of the Major Port Trust Act, 1963.

JAWAHARLAL NEHRU PORT TRUST EMPLOYEES (PAY AND ALLOWANCE) REGULATIONS, 1997.

section (1) of section 132 of the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 were examined and a questionnaire seeking some comments/clarifications was referred
to the Ministry of Surface Transport on January 27, 1999. The points raised in the questionnaire and the Ministry’s comments thereon as follows:-

Comments –
The Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust Employees (Pay and Allowances) Regulations, 1997 were laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on 27th July, 1998 and
Rajya Sabha on 28th July, 1998.
Question No. 2
Regulation 2(4) "Compensatory Allowance" means an allowance included in the Schedule or approved for inclusion in the Schedule or granted
under these or any other regulations to meet personal expenditure necessitated by the special circumstances in which duty is performed. It includes a
travelling allowance.
What is the justification for including travelling allowance within the meaning of the term "compensatory allowance" when the same has been
defined separately in regulation 2(28).
 
Comments-
The definition as contained in Regulation 2(4) of the JNP Employees (Pay & Allowances) Regulation, 1997 has been borrowed from the definition
of compensatory allowance as contained in the 9(5). This definition of compensatory allowance as contained in the Fundamental Rules specifically
states that it includes travelling allowance. In Regulation 2(28) of the JNP Regulations, travelling allowance has been separately defined as an
allowance granted to the employee to cover the expenditure which he incurs on travelling in the course of his employment and it includes allowance
granted for maintenance of any mode of conveyance. It may be seen that there is no duplication between Regulation 2(28) and Regulation 2(4)
which states that travelling allowance can also be treated as compensatory allowance.
Question No. 3
Regulation 2(19)- "Personal pay" means additional pay granted to an employee –
(i) to save him from a loss of substantive pay in respect of a permanent post due to revision of pay or to any reduction of such substantive pay
otherwise than as a disciplinary measure; or
(ii) in exceptional circumstances, on other personal consideration in accordance with the general orders issued by the Government as the case may
be.
The words "exceptional circumstances, on other personal consideration" appearing in the regulation does not appear to be specific. What are the
circumstances or personal consideration contemplated by the Ministry in this regulation. Whether there is any objection in making the regulation
specific and precise?
Comments-
Government has issued instructions for grant of a special increment in the form of personal pay in respect of employees who undergo sterilisation
operation after having 2 or 3 surviving children. Such personal pay should not be absorbed in further increases in pay either in the same post or on
promotion to a higher post. Such personal pay is also granted for passing certain specified Hindi examinations. It may not be advisable to elaborate
the words ‘exceptional circumstances on other personal consideration’ as it may not be possible to envisage all circumstances when Government
may issue instructions on granting of such personal pay in future. It is however, assured that there is not scope for misuse of this provisions, as such
personal pay can be granted only in accordance with the general orders issued by the government.
Question No. 4
Regulation 4 - Fixation of initial pay-
(I) The initial pay of an employee who is appointed to a post in the Board’s service on a time-scale of pay in regulated as follows:
(a)(i) Where an employee holding a post in a substantive, temporary or officiating capacity in the Board’s service in appointed in substantive,
temporary or officiating capacity as the case may be, subject to the fulfillment of the eligibility conditions as prescribed in the relevant Recruitment
Rules, to another post carrying duties an responsibilities of greater importance than those attaching to the post held by him, his initial pay in the
time-scale of the higher post shall be fixed at the stage next above the notional pay arrived at by increasing his pay in respect of the lower post held
by him regularly by an increment at the stage at which such pay has accrued or rupees twenty five only, whichever is more. Save incases of
appointment on deputation or foreign service to an ex-cadre post, or to a post on ad-hoc basis, the employee shall have

the option, to be exercised within one month from the date of appointment, to have the pay fixed under this regulation from the date of appointment
or to have the pay fixed initially at the stage of the time scale of the higher post above the regulation on the date of accrual of next increment in the
time scale of pay of the lower post. In cases where ad-hoc appointment is followed by regular appointment without break, the option is admissible
as from date of initial appointment to be exercised within one month from the date of regular appointment. Provided that where an employee is

in the time-scale of the higher post shall be fixed at the stage next above the pay notionally arrived at by increasing his pay in respect of the lower
post held by him on regular basis by an amount equal to the last increment in the time-scale of the lower post or rupees twenty-five, whichever is
more.
What is the justification for ensuring a minimum increase of Rs.25/- to an employee of the Port Trust while fixing his initial pay on initial
appointment? Whether this figure of Rs.25/- is common for pay fixation in all grades? When was the limit of Rs.25/- determined and whether a
revision of this amount is due or contemplated, if so, the details in this regard. What is the minimum rate of increment in the lowest grade in the Port
Trust.
Comments-
Rs.25 has been borrowed from Fundamental Rule 22 applicable to Central Govt. employees. This limit has been fixed to ensure certain minimum
increase of pay on promotion. It is applicable to all employees. The limit of Rs.25/- was introduced from 1
st January, 1986. The minimum rate of
increment applicable to port employees is Rs.35/-. It is due for revision from 1.1.97. It is felt that there is no need to stipulate minimum limit of
Rs.25/- now and hence the limit may be deleted.
Question No.5
Regulations 9 - Counting of service for increment
The following provisions prescribe the conditions on which service counts for increments in a time scale.
(1) XXX XXX XXX
All leave including extra-ordinary leave as defined in the JNPT Employees (Leave) Regulations taken on medical certificate, due to civil
commotion or for prosecuting higher technical and scientific studies and the period of deputation out of India shall count for increment in the time
scale applicable to the post which the employee was holding in regular or officiating capacity at the time he proceeded on leave or deputation out of
India and would have continued to officiate but for his proceeding on leave or deputation out of India.
Provided that where an employee takes extra-ordinary leave for any reasons beyond the control of the employee the Chairman may direct that such
extra-ordinary leave shall be counted for increments.
As per the proviso, the Chairman of the Board has been authorised to allow counting of extra ordinary leave for the purpose of increments in case
the extra ordinary leave is taken "for reasons beyond the control of the employee."
What are the situatio0ns contemplated to be covered by the above said proviso? The normal rule is that, extra-ordinary leave shall count for purpose
of increment only if the same is taken on Medical certificate. The words "for reasons beyond the control of the employee" are vague. Whether Govt.
have any objection in substituting them by some specific provision. Besides, the proviso vests wide discretionary powers in the Chairman of the
Board which are liable to he misused.
Comments-
Sub- regulation (2) specifies that extra ordinary leave taken on medical certificate, due to civil commotion and for prosecuting further studies will
count as duty for grant of annual increment. Other reasons which may justify extra-ordinary leave being counted as duty for increment are:
(i) Sudden failure of public transport system
(ii) Natural calamities like flood, etc.
It may not be advisable to delete the words "for reasons beyond the control of the employee" and substitute them by specific provisions as it may
not be possible to envisage all situations beyond the control of the employee for which counting of service for increment is justified.

Further the words "if the service be material" appearing in the Regulation is not specific and bestows wide discretion or the Port Trust. Whether this

1. Where an employee is permitted to perform a clerical, administrative or technical work of an occasional or casual nature in a purely Private
Body. The words ‘Private Body’ would include all Co-operative Societies registered under the Societies Registration Act which are not
subject to the administrative control of the Government.
2. Regular remunerative occupation in the nature of part-time employment permitted by JNPT.
3. Publishing a book or contributing an article on subjects other than literary, cultural or artistic, technological and scientific Management
Sciences, etc.
4. Where an employee receives sale proceeds or royalty on a book which is a mere compilation of Government Rules, Regulations and
Procedures.
5. Fee received by an employee from any University, Statutory Bodies, National Institute of Port Management, India Institute of Port
Management etc. The recovery of 1/3rd of the fee in excess of the limits mentioned has been provided to be in line with the Government
instructions on the subject, However, it is felt that there is no justification for such recovery. It will therefore be proposed to delete this

The words ‘if the service be material’ have been used to prevent any misuse of this provision. This is to ensure that the employee does not receive

Question No.8
Regulation 24 - Subsistence Allowance during suspension
2(ii) The subsistence allowance shall not be denied on any ground unless an employee is unable to/does not furnish a certificate that he is not
engaged in any other employment business, profession or vocation, during the period of suspension.
Regulation No.24 (2) (ii) is repetition of the conditions already prescribed under Regulation 24 (2) (i) what is the justification for adding Regulation
no24 (2) (ii) when the position already stands clarified in Regulation 24 (2) (i) whether the Ministry have any objection in avoiding this repetition?
Comments-
Regulation 24 (2) (i) says that subsistence allowance shall not be made unless the employee furnishes a certificate that he is not engaged in any
other employment, business, profession or vocation. Sub Clause (ii) of this sub regulation states that subsistence allowance shall not be denied on
any other ground other than non production of a certificate that he is not engaged in any employment etc. These provisions are slightly different
from each other. It is, however, proposed that sub-clause (ii) may be reworded to say that "the subsistence allowance shall not be denied to an
employee on any ground other than the non-production of certificate mentioned in sub-clause (i).
 
 
Question No.9-
Regulation 27(2)
Notwithstanding anything contained in Regulation 24 where an employee under suspension dies before the disciplinary or the Court proceedings
instituted against him are concluded, the period between the date of suspension and the date of death shall be treated as a period spent on duty for all
purposes and his family shall be paid the full pay, and allowances for that period to which he would have been entitled had he not been suspended,
subject to adjustment in respect of subsistence allowance already paid.
What is the justification in allowing the period between the date of suspension and the date of death of an suspended employee as period spent on
duty and allowing the benefits for all purposes?
Comments-
An employee may be suspended pending departmental enquiry or judicial proceedings. On conclusion of departmental enquiry or judicial
proceedings, suspension period is treated is duty, leave or no duty depending on the fact whether the employee was found guilty or not. If an
employee dies before conclusion of departmental enquiry or judicial proceedings such a conclusion cannot be made and therefore the suspension
period is treated as on duty as if he is not guilty. This provision is made to meet the principles of natural justice.

.

1.3     The notifications containing Rules/Regulations, etc. laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha during its 191st session have been perused by the
Committee in the light of the provisions of the Act under which they have been framed and also with a view to see whether they have been laid

REPORT
I
Laying of Statutory Orders on the Table of the Rajya Sabha
(191st Session)
        During the 191 st Session of  the Rajya Sabha, 205 Statutory Orders were laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha by the various
Ministries/Departments.  The details of the Gazette  Notifications in which these were published and the date of their laying on the Table of the
Rajya Sabha have been  indicated in the enclosed statement Ministrywise (Annexure).  Out of these 205 Orders, the Committee has identified six for
detailed scrutiny.  The Orders so identified  have been indicated in the statement.
 
2.
        During the course of general scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has come across several cases where there has been a considerable
time lag between the date of  notification of the Order and the date of its laying. The statement as at Annexure contains a specific mention of the
period of delay in cases where notifications have not been laid as per the Committee’s guidelines.  In many cases the delay is abnormal.  The
observations/recommendations of the Committee in this behalf are contained in the succeeding paragraphs.
 
        3.     The Committee is constrained to note that the Ministry of Finance has taken an unduly long time in laying a large number of regulations
(Sl. nos 32-52 of the Annexure) issued under the Foreign Exchange and Management  Act, 1999 that too without any delay statements. As may be
seen, all these notifications were published in the Gazette  in the first half  of May, 2000 and the Ministry of Finance could have laid these
notifications in the Monsoon Session of  the Rajya Sabha,  which was there  from July 24 to August 25, 2000.  Similarly, there has been a delay in
laying of the regulations at Sl. Nos.  53, 54, 55, 66 and 71 of the Annexure concerning Nationalized  Banks  which  were  also  laid  without  any 
delay  statements. 
 
The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Finance should avoid such delays in laying of such statutory orders before the
Parliament. 
 
4.
        In case of the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Committee regrets to note that there has been an unusually long delay ranging from  one year
to five years nine months in laying of Statutory Orders (Sl. No.107-111 of the Annexure) pertaining to Union Territories of Daman & Diu and
Andaman & Nicobar Islands issued under  the Regulations framed in exercise of powers conferred under Article  240  of the Constitution  of India. 
The Committee has  taken  a  serious  note  of this delay and also the fact that the Ministry of  Home Affairs  have not appended any statement
giving reasons for delay  while laying  these Statutory Orders.  The Committee would like the Ministry of Home Affairs to avoid recurrence of such
instances for future.
                       5.     Similarly,  The Ministry of Rural Development have also delayed the laying  of Statutory Orders (Sl. 166-168 of the Annexure)
concerning Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu issued under Regulations framed in exercise of powers conferred by Article 240 of the

132

Constitution.  In this case also, the delay is even greater ranging from four years seventeen  days to five years ten months. The Ministry of Rural
Development have also not appended any delay statement while laying of these Statutory Orders.  The Committee takes a serious note of these
cases of extreme delay in laying of Statutory Orders before the Parliament.  The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Rural Development would
take due precaution to avoid recurrence of such instances.
               
        6.     The Committee would like to impress upon all the Ministries/Departments to avoid delay in  the laying of Statutory Orders before
Parliament. With a view to ensure  this  the  Committee  reiterates  its
observation made in its 131
st Report that Orders framed under any Central Act, should be laid on the Table of the House in compliance with the
provisions of the Act on the first available opportunity. The Committee further reiterates its following recommendation as contained in the said
report which lay down the time schedule  for the Ministry/Departments of Government of India in the matter of laying of Statutory Orders:-
 
“Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid  (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session immediately following the
date of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is  in Session, on the date of the  publication of  the Order,
during its continuance and in case the time  lag  between  the  date  of  publication  and  the  date  of  the
 
closing  of the Session is less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the Session immediately following the said Session.  All the
Ministries/Departments of Government of India should henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of the orders issued
under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.”
 
7.
        While scrutinizing  the Orders the Committee also examined the aspect whether the original orders that have been laid during the Session
have been framed under the appropriate authority of the concerned Act.  The Committee notes with satisfaction that these Orders have been framed
within the parameters prescribed under the relevant Acts.

INTRODUCTION
 
 
        I,      the Chairman of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, having been authorized by the Committee to
present the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this Hundred and Fortieth Report of the Committee.
 
        1.2   The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on February 11, 2002.
 
        1.3           The matter examined by the Committee arises out of the scrutiny of concerned Rules/Regulations
relating to the subject along with the Government’s comments received thereon.  The Committees’
observations/recommendations are contained in the Report that follows.
 
 
 
DIPANKAR   MUKHERJEE
Chairman
NEW DELHI                                                                                                                                            Committee on Subordinate Legislation,
February 11, 2002                                                                                                                                                                                  Rajya Sabha
                                         
                                                                                               
Report
 
I
 
Ministry of Finance Notification S.O. No. 995(E) dated 3rd November, 2000 regarding approval of GIC as Indian
Reinsurer under section 101A(8)(ii) of the Insurance Act, 1938-Implementation of 134th Report of the Committee on
Subordinate Legislation, Rajya Sabha.
 
      The Committee in its 134th Report presented to the House on 25th April, 2001 inter-alia dealt with the matter relating to Notification S. O. No.
995 (E) dated 3rd November 2000 issued by the Ministry of Finance (Annexure I) which had effect of restricting activities of the GIC in the area of
reinsurance only without formally amending the General Insurance Business (Nationalization) Act, 1972.  The Committee after examining the
subject matter observed as follows:
 
“that issue of notification S.O. 995(E) dated 3rd November 2000 which has the effect of restricting the activates of
GIC to the area of reinsurance, without   formally amending the parent Act was not a well considered course of
action on the part of the Ministry of Finance. In Committee’s views, the reasons advanced by the Ministry of
Finance that it is a requirement of law and the IRDA was insisting upon the issue are not convincing enough for
action in such a manner by the Ministry. The Committee is of the view that issue of notification before formally
amending the parent Act was putting the cart before the horse. The Committee also observed that the objectives of
Bill to entrust the task of Indian reinsurer to General Insurance Corporation and delink General Insurance
Corporation from its subsidiaries by carrying out necessary amendments in the GIBN Act 1972 as mentioned in the
Statement of Objects and Reason have already been brought into effect by the Ministry through the notification
followed by the administrative instructions of November 7, 2000. The effect of the notification was to take

140
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/140th.htm[25-10-2016 16:41:14]
advantage of a loophole in the Act to nullify the basic provisions of the Act, and in the Committee’s opinion  the 
action   and  the manner  in  which   it was  achieved constitutes an attempt to bypass the authority of Parliament.
That   this   was  realized   by   the   Ministry   is   clear  from  the subsequent introduction of a Bill on the same subject. The
Committee strongly deprecates the entire episode and trusts that Government will ensure that cases of this kind do not occur in future”.
 
2.     The fact that the General Insurance Business (Nationalization) Amendment Bill 2001 which was  introduced in the
Lok Sabha on 12.03.2001 was still pending gave an  impression as if the change in the role of GIC was being managed

The Bank (Officer’s) Service Regulations, 1979 - 
Implementation of the recommendations of the 
Committee as contained in its 124th Report. 
 
 
 The Committee in its 124 th Report presented to the 
House on April 23, 1999 ha d inter-alia examined the Bank 
(Officer’s) Service Regulations, 1979 of the Subsidiary Bank 
of State Bank of India, viz the State Bank of Travancore and 
the State Bank of Mysore framed under the State Bank of 
India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959.  The Commit tee in its 
Report had recommended as under: 
 
 (i)  Regulation 50(3) 
 
The Committee had a detailed discussion on the 
provisions of Regulation 50(3).  It was convinced that the 
directions from the superior official under this regulation 
could not always be i n writing.  But, in the opinion of the 
Committee, there should be no objection to the confirmation 
of such oral directions in writing at the earliest available 
opportunity.  The Committee recommends that the regulation 
be amended, accordingly. 
 
(ii)  Regulation 50(4)   
 
The Committee considered the views of the Ministry of 
Finance as well as the views of the State Bank of Mysore on the 
Committee’s suggestion to replace the words “Bank Official” 
by the word “Officer” and recommended that the Committee’s 
suggestion for suitable modification of regulation 50(4) which 
has been accepted by the Ministry of Finance should be acted 
upon and the regulation may be modified suitably. 
 

(iii) Regulation 51(1) 
 
The Committee expresses its satisfaction that the 
representatives of both the Banks have, during the course of 
discussion, agreed to the suggestion of the Committee that the 
reasons for directing a Bank Official to discontinue any work 
of social or charitable nature should be recorded in writing .  
The Committee recommends that the suitable action may be 
taken for amendment of the regulation 51(1). 
(iv) Regulation 51(4) 
 
The Committee notes with satisfaction that the 
Ministry of Finance as well as the representatives of the banks 
have agreed to replace the word “fee” by the word “payment” 
which is more appropriate.  It hopes that suitable amendments 
would be carried out expeditiously. 
 
(v) Regulation 54, 64(1) & (2) 
 
The Committee notes the explanation furnished by the 
Ministry of Finance as well as the representatives of the banks 
on Regulations 54, 64(1)and (2) and decides that the 
regulations may remain in their existing form .”

4.1 Point referred  
Regulation 15: Proviso 
 
This proviso creates disparity among the Bank  Officers 
and directly affects the spirit of equality under article 14 of the 
Indian Constitution.  Whether the Ministry have any objection 
to specify the conditions under which the probation period of 
a particular officer will be reduced or dispensed with? 
 
Comments of the Bank 
 
  Probationary Officers who are entering the  Bank’s  
service for the first time have to be adequately trained 
before they are entrusted with responsible assignments.  
Similarly Trainee Officers (Group  B Officers)  considering 
their limited exposure to various spheres of banking 
activity are also pu t under training for a   period of one 
year.  Taking into account the nature of appointment of 
these category of officers, the probation period has been  
prescribed as two years as against one year for other 
promoted officers.  Even though probation period  has  
prescribed  as two years and one year for probationary 

officers, Trainee Officers and one year for other  
promotees respectively  for all purposes viz., increment, 
seniority, and promotion it is their date of 
appointment/date of promotion which are t aken into 
account and not the date of confirmation,  for determining 
their consequential benefits.  Therefore, fixation of 
different probation period for different category of officers 
is related to needs of training/job requirements and does 
not amount to  violation of Article 14 of the Constitution.

  This regulation in principle provides an opportunity to

Bank.  Any person who, immediately prior to the 
appointed date was an officer of the Bank, upon 
implementation of the regulations will be “fitted” in the 
new pay scale.  The wor d “fitted” used in the definition 
thus differentiates persons in the service of the Bank 
immediately prior to the appointed date and those who are 
subsequently appointed/promoted as officers. 
 
5.4 Point referred Regulation 16 (1) 
 
This sub -regulation provi des that a probationary 
officer shall be confirmed in the service of the Bank if, in the 
opinion of the competent authority, the officer has 
satisfactorily completed the training in any institution to which 
the officer may have been deputed for  training a nd the in -
service training in the Bank and the proviso to the sub -
regulation provides that an officer directly recruited to the 

Junior Management grade may be required also to pass a test 
in a language other than his mother tongue.  
 
What will be the crite ria to judge that the officer has 
satisfactorily completed the training and what will be the basis 
of the “opinion” of the competent authority? Whether it will 
be the assessment report of the institution that has imparted 
training to the officer or the ass essment report of the team 
imparting in-service training in the Bank.  The regulation is 
not clear.  Whether the Ministry would like to make it  more 
comprehensive to remove these anomalies? 
 
Similarly the proviso to the regulation is also not clear.  
Whether the officer has to pass a written test or an oral test 
in a language other than his mother tongue?  Whether this 
provision is being resorted to?  Will the Ministry clarify this 
aspect in the regulation itself? 
 
Comments of the Bank 
   
The Training sche dule of Probationary Officers 
contains only eight weeks of institutional training.  During the 
entire remaining period the trainee undergoes a well 
structured on the job training.  The Trainees are required to 
submit a monthly diary detailing therein vario us fields of 
training undergone by him/her during the month under 
reference.  This diary would be reviewed by the Branch 
manager/HRD Department at Head Office and deficiencies 
observed brought to the notice of the Trainee.  Further, 
Annual confidential rep ort is also written on the trainees by 
the Branch Manager/Head of the Department and reviewed by 
HRD Department at head Office.  These officers are always 
under close watch and guidance and their performance is 
monitored.  These points of control would for m an “opinion” 
and would facilitate an evaluation by the competent Authority. 

  
As Banking is a service industry the officers including 
the trainees have to interact very closely with the local 
population and in the process pick up the local language, at 
least the basics, quite fast.  In fact as they are transferred 
through out the country many pick up many languages.  As the 
purpose of the provision is thus met no specific language test 
is administered to them. 
 
5.5 Point referred Regulation 20 (2) 
 
The second proviso to the sub-regulation provides that 
the competent authority, may, at its discretion, permit an 
officer to resign without notice or forfeiture of security deposit 
or payment in lieu of notice or reduce the  period of notice. 
 
What are the  circumstances in which an officer could 
be permitted to resign without notice on forfeiture of security 
deposit or payment in lieu of notice or reduce the  period of 
notice?  Whether there is any objection in incorporating of the 
same in the  Regulation itself? 
 
Comments of the Bank 
 
  Normally an officer is not permitted to resign without 
notice or forfeiture of security or with reduced notice 
period or with payment in lieu of notice.  In exceptional 
circumstances like taking up assignments with State Ban k 
of India, Reserve Bank of India, other apex level financial 
institutions etc. the competent authority may consider 
waiver of the above condition. 
 
5.6 Point referred Regulation 29 
 

This Regulation provides that the Bank may reimburse 
to an Officer such enter tainment expenses and such fees for 
membership of clubs and professional institutions as may be 
decided by the Board or the Executive Committee in 
accordance with the State Bank’s guidelines. 
 
What is the justification of providing this Regulation? 
Why the terms “entertainment” and “clubs” and “professional 
institutions” have not been defined in the Regulations?  
Whether the Ministry would like to make the provision more 
clear?  Whether Government have issued some guidelines on 
this aspect; if so, what are the details? 
 
Comments of the Bank 
 
  The Bank being basically a commercial institution can 
thrive only by obtaining timely market information and 
intelligence in view of the intense competition in the field. 
“Clubs” and “Professional Institutions” are the  
appropriate “fora’ where Bank officers are able to meet 
prospective customers and access information regarding 
the market and its developments.  It also facilitates creation 
of new business connections.  The entertainment expenses 
are restricted and are m ade available strictly on the basis 
of guidelines issued by Government vide memorandum No. 
3/15/79-BPE(WC) dated 09.04.1984 from Bureau of Public 
Enterprises, New Delhi.  
 
5.7 Point referred Regulation 36 
 
This Regulation provides that leave up to a period of 3 
months at a time may be granted by way of maternity leave 
including in respect of postnatal period or at the time of 
miscarriage or abortion, so however, that no more than 12 

months of such leave shal l be available during the  entire 
period of service of the officer. 
 
The Regulation gives an impression that the female 
employees are entitled to take maternity leave on four 
occasions, not exceeding 12 months period during the entire 
period of service.  W hether the Ministry has any objection in 
clarifying the same? 
 
Comments of the Banks 
 
  The provisions of the regulation are not against the 
Government Policy on Family Planning.  In fact, by 
extending the provisions to cover abortions also Bank is 
encouraging Government’s Family Planning Policies. 
 
5.8 Point referred: Regulation 38 
 
The Regulation begins with the words 
  
“All leave shall lapse on the death of the officer” and 
the proviso states that where an officer retires from the Bank’s 
Service, he shall be eligible to be paid a sum equivalent to the 
emoluments of any  period of privilege  leave that he has 
accumulated. 
 
“The words ‘shall lapse on the death of the officer or if 
he ceases to be in the service of the Bank’ and  ‘shall be eligible 
to be paid a sum equivalent to the emoluments of any  period 
of privilege leave that he has accumulated’ are inherently 
contradictory in nature.  Whether the Ministry have any 
objection in modifying the regulation accordingly? 
 
Comments of the Bank 
 

  Regulation 38 pro vides the general rule that all leave 
shall lapse on the death or cessation of employment of an 
officer.  The general rule is subject to two exemptions 
stated in the provisions.  The first exemption is that leave 
salary equivalent to the privilege leave at  credit shall be 
payable to the legal representatives of the officer on his 
death while in employment.  The second exemption is that 
the office retiring from service shall be eligible to be paid 
leave salary equivalent to the privilege leave at credit upto 
240 days.  Under the circumstances no modification to the 
regulation seems necessary.  
 
5.9 Point referred Regulation 39 
 
It has been  provided by this regulation that an officer on 
leave may be recalled to duty by the  competent authority 
whenever the Bank deems fit to do so.  But, if the officer is 
at that time out of station, he shall be eligible to be paid 
the actual expenses incurred by him and the members of 
his family for coming back to the station and if the officer 
and the members of his family go back to the same station 
from which he was called, for the return journey also.” 
 
  The regulations gives an impression that an officer who 
was availing leave with his family at a distant place from 
the place of duty, in case of recall   to duty, returned to the 
same place where he was availing leave with his family be 
eligible to be paid the actual expenses incurred by him and 
the members of his family which should not be permitted.  
Whether the Ministry have any objection in amending the 
regulation suitably? 
 
Comments of the Bank 
 

  As the officer is being recalled for duty by the 
competent Authority from a vacation he was enjoying with 
his family, it would be fair to pay the actual expenses 
incurred by him and the members of his family for coming 
back to headquarters and if there is any residual unutilized 
leave portion, for going back to the same station from 
where the officer was recalled. 
 
5.10 Point referred Regulation 41 
  
In sub-regulations (i)  and (ii) it has been provided that 
officers of Junior and Middle Management Grade may travel 
by Ist  Class or AC Sleeper by train.  Since the AC Sleeper has 
been bifurcated into  2 tier and 3 tier categories in most of the 
trains, this sub -regulation may be amended to specify the  
category of AC Sleeper according to the entitlement of the 
Junior and Middle Management Grade Officers respectively. 
 
 Whether the Ministry have any objection in doing so? 
 
 
Comments of the Bank 
 
  The regulation provides that Officers in Junior and 
Middle Management Grades may travel by First Class or 
A/C sleeper by train.  As three tier A/C sleeper class is a 
recent introduction and majority of the trains running 
across the country do  not have three tier A/C Sleeper class 
facility, eligibility of A/C Sleeper two tier is being extended 
to all officers in Junior management and Middle 
Management Grades. 
 
5.11 Point referred Regulation 75 
 

This Regulation provides that the Managing Director  
may, from time to time, issue such instructions or directions as 
may, in his opinion, be necessary for giving effect to or 
carrying out the provision of these Regulations. 
 
The Power to implement the Regulations, it is felt, 
should not vest in the Managing Director alone because that 
could lead to arbit rariness.  Instead, the powers including 
appellate power, wherever necessary, should lie with the  
Board. 
 
 Whether the Ministry have any objection in amending the 
Regulation accordingly? 
 
Comments of the Bank 
 
  The power given to the Managing Director is  only to 
issue instructions to implement the regulations as the 
executive head of the Bank and this is in line with section 
29 of State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959. It 
may not perhaps be practical to have the powers shifted to 
the Chairman (who is also the Chairman of state Bank of 
India and all other Associates and Subsidiaries) or the 
Board in which case every issue whether important or 
unimportant will have to be referred to the Board leading 
to administrative delays adversely affecting th e 
effectiveness of the Executive Head. Further, regulation 77 
vests the powers for application or interpretation of any of 
the provisions of the regulations with the Board or the 
Executive Committee. We are therefore, of the view that 
the present arrangement may be permitted to continue.

contained in the  106th Report would be sent to the Secretariat

respectively.  Thereafter, reminders were issued on 
Committees’ behalf to which the Ministry failed to respond.  A 
D.O. letter dated 19 th June, 1998 from the Chairman of the 
Committee was also sent to the then Minister of Finance 
drawing his attention to the inordinate delay on the part of the 
Ministry in responding to the  communications issued on 
behalf of the Committee.  However, no reply was forthcoming. 
 
4. The Committee at its meeting held on September 14, 1999 
took a serious view on the  laxity on the part of the Ministry in 
the matter and decided to call the Secretary, Ministry of 
Finance before the Committee. 
 
In the meantime , the Ministry of Finance furnished the 
Action Taken Note on the recommendation of the Committee 
vide their communication dated 26th May, 2000. The 
Committee at its meeting held on 12th October, 2001 
considered the subject matter.  The Committee  accepted the 
position as stated by the Ministry of Finance on the 
recommendations  relating to Regulation 4 regarding deletion 
of the words ‘or for any other good or sufficient reasons’ and 
giving comprehensive definition of the word ‘misconduct’; 
regulation 54(4)  regarding the  acts ‘unbecoming of an 
officer’; and regulation 67 regarding classification of acts of 
misconduct  attracting minor penalties and acts of 
misconduct  attracting major penalties and decided not to 
pursue the same. The Committee, however, noted with 
satisfaction that the Ministry have accepted/taken action on 
the various recommendations of  the Committee as indicated 
below: 
 
I. Committee’s recommendation (Para 2.23) 
 
During the course of discussion with various Officer’s  
Association of the Banks, the Committee was informed that the 

‘Sealed Cover Procedure’ for promotion should be dropped 
altogether, thus ensuring promotion for all eligible and 
deserving officers.  The Committee observed that Sealed cover 
Procedure is being followed in  all the public sector banks in 
terms of which promotion result of an Officer against whom 
disciplinary action has been initiated is placed in a sealed 
cover.  The sealed cover is opened only after the disciplinary 
proceedings concluded.  The Committee was informed that an 
order on ‘Sealed Cover Procedure’ was issued by the 
Government in September, 1992 and the same was circulated 
to all the Banks also. The Committee notes that the said 
circular takes care of the subject and recommends that the 
procedure th us evolved should be followed by the 
managements of all the Banks.  
 
Action Taken  
 
  The observations of the Committee have been noted.  The 
Banks are already following the procedure.  
 
II. Committee’s recommendations (Para 2.24) 
 
There should be strict restriction on issuing of order of 
suspension. The  Committee  also observed that officer 
employees who are detained by the police for a period 
exceeding 48 hours are suspended by the management 
automatically but there is no provision for subsequent 
reinstatement on their release.  Instances were brought before 
the Committee that employees who are cleared of the charges 
or acquitted of the charges are not reinstated after the 
trail/inquiry was over.  It was also brought to the notice of the 
Committee that even after detention for 48 hours though there 
was no filing of charge sheet or  
Court Proceedings, reinstatement had not taken place.  The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that in such like cases the 

Provision of reinstatement in the rules should be incorporated 
expeditiously so that the officer employees who are cleared 
from the charges are reinstated without any delay. 
 
Action Taken 
 
 The Committee’s recommendation is in the specific context 
of cases where reinstatement had not taken place even though 
no charge sheet or court proceedings were filed even after 
detention for 48 hours and it is not so much for incorporating 
a provision for automatic reinstatement.  The Regulations 
already contain provision for modification or revocation of the 
suspension order.  On revocation, the officer employee would 
be reinstated in the bank’s service.  However, revocation of the 
suspension order has to be considered on the facts and 
circumstances of the case.  
 
 Government have already in June, 1981 issued detailed 
guidelines regarding periodic review of cases of officials who 
have been placed under suspension.  A copy of these guidelines 
is enclosed at Annexure.  In para (d) of these guidelines it has 
inter alia been stated- 
 
‘as soon as an official is released from po lice custody 
the competent authority should consider the case to 
decide whether the continuance of the official under 
suspension is absolutely necessary or not.’ 
 
 Keeping in view the specific recommendation of the 
Committee, Government proposes to examine the issue further 
and issue specific guidelines in this regard in consultation with 
Ministry of law and Justice.  
 
III. Committee’s recommendations (Para 2.26) 
 

The Committee also observed that 45 days time limit 
has been fixed for filing an appeal against an order of 
Disciplinary Authority but in some of the banks there is no 
time limit for disposal of such appeals by the Appellate 
Authority.  The Committee, during the course of discussions 
with the managements was informed that some of the 
managements have provision for disposal of appeals within 90 
days.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the 
managements of all the Banks should uniformly follow the 
practice of disposing the appeals within 90 days.   
 
Action Taken 
 
 Government is in agreement in princi ple that there 
should be uniformity in this regard in all banks.  The matter 
would be processed further in consultation with RBI and IBA.  
 
6. The Committee notes with satisfaction that the 
managements of all the Banks are already following the 
‘Sealed Cover Procedure’ as recommended by the Committee 
(para 2.23). The Committee hopes that the Ministry would 
issue specific guidelines in the matter of reinstatement of the 
officer who had been placed under suspension for being in 
police custody beyond 48 hours but later on cleared of the 
charges after trial/inquiry and intimate about the same to it. 
The Committee reiterates that the managements of all the 
Banks should follow uniformly the practice of disposing the 
appeals within 90 days and hopes that the Ministry/ RBI/ IBA 
shall comply with its recommendation in this regard. The 
Committee, however, takes a serious exception over the 
unduly long time being taken by the Ministry in responding to 
its communications/recommendations and directs them to act 
promptly in such matters in future.  
 
 

Annexure 
(vide para 5 part II, page 46) 
 
 Letter No.1/33/81-Vigilance dated 29.6.81 issued by the 
Ministry of Finance Department of Economic Affairs 
(Banking Division) to the Chairman & Managing Director of 
the nationalized banks.  
 
Subject:  Suspension of officials of public sector 
banks - periodic review of their cases 
(Guidelines) 
   
Sir, 
 
 I am directed to say that several cases have come to the 
notice of the Government where the bank officials facing 
departmental/criminal proceedings have been kept under 
suspension for excessively long periods.  Though suspension is 
not a punishment, it certainly constitutes a great hardship  for 
the  concerned official. In fairness to him it is necessary   that 
the pe riod of suspension should conform to the barest 
minimum.  In this context the following instructions are 
reiterated for guidance and strict compliance:- 
 
(a) An official may generally be placed under suspension 
only in the following circumstances:- 
 
(i) where the continuance in office of the official 
will lead to prejudice investigation, trial or any 
inquiry (e.g. apprehended tampering with 
witnesses or documents); 
 
(ii) where the continuance in  office of the official is 
likely to seriously subvert discipline in the office 
in which he is working; 

 
(iii) where the continuance in office of the official 
will be against, wider  public interest, e.g. if 
there is a public scandal and it is considered 
necessary to place the official under suspension 
to demonstrate the policy of the bank to deal 
strictly with officers involved in such scandals,  
particularly  corruption. 
 
(iv) where preliminary, enquiry into allegations 
made has revealed a prima facie case justifying 
criminal or departmental proceedings which are 
likely to lead to his conv iction and or dismissal 
removal or compulsory retirement from  
service;  and  
 
(v) where the official is suspected to have engaged 
himself in activities prejudicial  to the interest of 
the security of the state. 
 
(b) Even in the above circumstance, an official may  be 
placed under suspension only in respect of misdemeanor of the 
following type: 
 
(i) an offence of conduct involving moral turpitude. 
 
(ii) corruption, embezzlement or misappropriation 
bank money, possession of disproportionate 
assets, misuse of official power of personal 
gains; 
 
(iii) services abandonment of official duty causing 
great loss to the Bank. 
 
(iv) Flight from duty; and  

 
(v) “refusals or caliberate failure to carry out 
written orders of supervisory officers. 
 
(c) While placing an official under suspension the 
competent authority should consider whether the 
purpose cannot be served by transferring the official 
from his post  to a post where be may not repeat the 
misconduct or influence the investigations, i f any, in 
progress.  If the authority finds that the purpose cannot 
be served by transferring the official from his post to 
another post then he should record reasons therefore, 
before placing the official under suspension. 
 
(d) In case where an official is deemed to have been placed 
under suspension under Discipline and Appeal 
Regulations etc, as soon as the official is released from 
the police custody the competent authority should 
consider the case to decide whether the continuance of 
the official under suspension is absolutely necessary or 
not.  If the period of suspension has already exceeded 
the limit of three months and the competent authority 
does not find justification to revoke the suspension in 
such  case he should immediately make a report to the 
next higher authority giving detailed justification for 
continuing the official under suspension. 
 
(e) In order keep the period of suspension to the barest 
minimum the competent authority should take all 
possible steps to file a charge sheet in a court of law, 
where an official has been placed under suspension on 
account of a court case or serve the chargesheet if the 
action is to be taken under the Discipline and Appeal 
Regulations within three months from the date of 
suspension and in case it is not possible to do so to 

report the matter to higher authorities explaining  the 
reasons for delay. 
 
(f) In respect of cases other than those pending in courts, 
the total period of suspension should not ordinarily 
exceed six months except in exceptional cases where it 
is not possible to adhere to this time limit then the 
competent authority should make a report to the next 
higher authority exploring the reasons for delay. 
 
(g) All authorities receiving information/report about the 
continued suspension of officials from their 
subordinate authorities should carefully examine each 
case and see whether the continued suspension of an 
official is absolutely necessary or the suspension should 
be revoked by transferring the official to another post 
of office. 
 
In order to ensure that the above instructions are 
scrupulously observed by subordinate authorities; all cases of 
suspension may please be reviewed regularly, at intervals of 
six months, particularly those where officials are under 
suspension  for more than six months, and wherever it is 
found that the official can be allowed to resume duties by 
transferring him from his post to another post and where 
necessary in consultation with CBI/CID/Police or other 
appreciate agencies, order  should be issued for revoking the 
suspension and allowing the official to resume duties with 
further direction as may be considered desirable in each 
individual case.  The review should not, however, be done in 
a repressed way and it should be borne in mind that 
revocation of suspension does not prejudice the criminal or 
Departmental Proceedings.  
 
The receipt of this letter may kindly be acknowledged.

VII 
Banking Service Commission Act, 1984-Delay in framing of 
Rules/Regulations 
 
 
 The Banking Service Commission  Act was enacted in 
the year 1984.  But till date, the Act has not been enforced by 
the Ministry of Finance.  The Committee on Subordinate 
Legislation, Rajya Sabha which dealt with the subject and in 
its 101 st Report presented to the House on 26 th April, 1 994 
inter-alia examined the aspect of delay in framing of 
rules/regulation under the said Act.  The Committee’s 
observations/recommendations as contained in its 101st Report 
are reproduced below: 
 
“2.10 The Committee notes with deep concern the fact 
that the Banking Service Commission Act, 1984 
has not been enforced even after more than 9 
years. 
 
2.11 The Committee takes serious view of the fact 
that the Ministry have given a routine and even 
contradictory information.   On the one hand, 
they intimated that “act ion has already been 
initiated for setting up of the Banking Service 
Commission and for framing rules under 
Section 31 of the Act” which was further 
supplemented that “the question of appointment 
of Chairman and members of the Commission 
after which the Act would be brought into force 
is under consideration at the highest level in the 
Government”. On the other hand the Ministry, 
subsequently intimated that “the question 
whether the Act should be got repealed or 

continue to be held in abeyance is engaging th e 
attention of the Government”.  The Committee 
feels that the Ministry owes an explanation for 
this. 
 
2.12 The Committee is of the considered view that 
though the timing of giving effect to an Act of 
Parliament is the discretion of the 
Administrative Ministry, it is, however, not the 
intention of Parliament that the Government 
should keep an Act passed by both the Houses of 
Parliament and assented to by the President, in 
limbo for such a long time. 
2.13 The Committee is constrained to observe that 
while the Government has shown great alacrity 
in getting the Bill passed by the Parliament, it is 
strange that the Government drags its feet in the 
implementation of the Act. 
 
2.14 The Committee, therefore, recommends that 
after reviewing the matter either the Act be 
enforced or be got repealed within a period of 
six months and the Committee be informed, 
accordingly.  The Committee is not inclined to 
grant any further extension of time in this 
regard. 
 
2. The Ministry of Finance had informed on the 24 th 
April, 1995 that a Committee had been setup under the 
Chairmanship of Shri D.R. Mehta,  then Deputy Governor of 
the Reserve Bank of India, to review the necessity to setup of a 
Banking Service Commission. 
 
3. In 1996 the Mehta Committee had submitted its Report 
recommending that the Banking Service Commission Act, 

1984 may be repealed.  The Ministry sought extension of time 
up to 30 -9-1996 stating that the Report of the Mehta 
Committee was under examination.  The Ministry was granted 
further another extension of time up to 30-9-1997. 
 
4. The Ministry of Finance informed on the 16 th 
September, 1998 that the Committee setup by the Government 
on Banking Sector reforms under the Chairmanship of Sh. M. 
Narsimhain,  in its report submitted to Government, had made 
various recommendations requiring changes in the legal 
framework of Banking industry and the recommendations of 
this Committee were under examination alongwith the 
decisions to repeal the Banking Service Commission Act,  
1984.  With this the Ministry sought another extension of time 
up 31-12-1998. 
 
5. The Ministry of Finance in their communication dated 
the 24th December, 1998 stated that the Minister had given in 
principal, approval for repealing of the Banking Service 
Commission Act, 1984 and the steps were bei ng taken to 
complete the formalities to repeal the same.  The Ministry was 
again granted extension of time upto 31.3. 1999 to complete the 
process.  Thereafter, the Ministry was given further extension 
thrice upto 31.6.1999, 31.12.1999 and 30.6.2000, respectively to 
complete the process of repealing the Act. 
 
6. In their communication dated 17 th July 2000 the 
Ministry stated as under:- 
 
“After the reform process initiated in early 1990s, 
banks are passing through transition phase during 
which drastic changes are taking place in their manner 
of working, operations, recruitment policies, staffing 
norms etc.  Besides, in the context of technological up -
gradation, there would be need to reassess the 

manpower requirement particularly of those 
possessing requisite sk ills.  Under the above 
circumstances, Government would like to wait for some 
more time before taking a decision on repealing the Act 
or framing of rules/Regulations there under and 
reassess the situation after a few years” 
 
7. The Ministry of Finance (Banking Division) in their last 
communication dated March 26, 2001 informed as: 
 
 “The proposal for abolition of the Banking Service 
Recruitment Boards is under examination and 
modalities for implementing the same are in process in 
consultation with Reserve Bank of India/Indian Banks 
Association.  After the action on this issue is complete 
Government will consider the question of repealing or 
retention of the Banking Service Commission Act, 
1984, the process is expected to get completed by July 
2001”. 
  
8. The Committee notes that the Ministry of Finance have 
in the meantime introduced a Bill in Lok Sabha in March, 2002  
with the objective of repealing the Banking Service 
Commission Act 1984.  The Committee, however, feels that lot 
of time has elapsed even after the introduction of the Bill.  The 
Committee, accordingly desires that the Ministry should 
expedite their action in the matter.

Rajya Sabha during its 195th  session have been perused by the Committee in the light 
of the provisions of the Acts under which these have been framed and also with a view

NEW DELHI  
,  2002 
A. VIJAYA RAGHAVAN 
 Chairman 
Committee on Subordinate Legislation 
Rajya Sabha 
 
 
  
 
  
  
Report 
  
I 
Laying of Statutory Orders on the Table of  Rajya Sabha 
  
  
            During the 195th Session of the Rajya Sabha, 267 Statutory Orders were laid 
on the Table of the House by the various Ministries/Departments.   The details of the 
Gazette Notifications in which these were published & the date of their laying on th e 
Table of the Rajya Sabha have been indicted in the enclosed Ministry wise statement 
(Annexure). 
  
2.         During the course of general scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has 
noted some cases where there has been a considerable time lag between th e date of 
notification of the Order and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also 
indicates the period of delay in cases where notifications have not been laid as per the 
Committee’s guidelines.  In some of the cases the delay has been quite abnormal.  The 
observations/ recommendations of the Committee respect of specific 
Ministries/Departments are as follows:- 
             
i.         Ministry of Commerce & Industry  
The Committee notes that the Ministry of Commerce and Industry have laid 
on the Table of the Rajya Sabha the Tobacco Board (Recruitment) Regulations, 1984 
as well as the Tobacco Board (Recruitment) Regulations, 1989 just because it was not 
possible for them to confirm beyond doubt whether these regulations had been laid 

before both House of Parliament earlier as the relevant records were not traceable. 
The Committee, while it appreciates the initiative of the Ministry, but, at the same 
time, it expects them to set right their records relating to the framing and the laying 
of subordinate legislation under various Acts being administered by them at-least for 
future so that such situations are avoided. 
  
ii.         Ministry of Communication and Information Technology 
            The Committee regrets to find that out of the five notifications laid by the 
Ministry of Communication and Information Technology, there has been a delay in 
case of two (sl. nos. 27 and 28 of the Annexure). The Committee expects the Ministry 
of Communication, etc. to exercise caution in such matters for future and ensure that 
the schedule as prescribed by the Committee in the matter of laying of subordinate 
legislation framed under various Acts of Parliament is followed meticulously from 
time to time. 
  
iii.        Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution 
                        The Committee regrets to note that out of 15 notifications, there has 
been a delay in laying of seven as mentioned at sl. Nos. 4,5,6,9,10, 11 and 17A of the 
Annexure. The Committee would like the Ministry of Consume r Affairs, etc. to take 
steps to avoid recurrence of such instances and ensure the compliance of the schedule 
as laid down by the Committee in the matter of laying of rules/regulations, etc. in its 
131st and 135th Reports. 
  
iv.        Ministry of Finance 
                        The Committee deeply regrets to note that for the sixth consecutive 
Session, the Ministry of Finance is coming under its particular notice due to delay in 
the laying of subordinate legislation on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. Ironic ally, the 
magnitude of the default is larger this time. The Ministry have laid 184 
rules/regulations during the 195th Session and there has been delay in case of 141 (sl. 
nos. 34, 37 39 -80, 94 -130, 135 -160, 172, 173,174, 176 -197 and 226 -227 of the 
Annexure). The Committee is even further pained to note the period by which the 
laying has been delayed which roughly averages anywhere between 8 –12 months. In 

the opinion of the Committee, calls for immediate corrective action. The Committee 
directs the Ministry of Finance to take action to prevent such lapses in the future. 
  
v.         Ministry of Home Affairs 
                        The Committee notes with regret that out of the seven notifications laid 
by the Ministry of Home Affairs during the 195 th Session, there has been a delay in 
case of five. In case of the Central Industrial Security Force Group “A” and   “B” 
Civilian Gazetted Posts Recruitment Rules, 2000, the delay is as long as of eleven 
months. The Committee would like the Ministry of Home Affairs to have a relook into 
the internal mechanism in place so as to obviate such instances for the future. 
  
vi.        Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of 1 year and 2 
months on the part of Minist ry of Information & Broadcasting in laying their only 
notification, namely, the Prasar Bharati (Broadcasting Corporation of India) 
(Audience Research Posts) Service Regulations (Sl. No. 245). 
             
The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting would 
take due care & ensure prompt compliance of the schedule prescribed by the 
Committee for the purpose. 
  
vii.       Ministry of Labour 
                        The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Labour have laid 
two notifications during the 195th Session and there has been a delay in both the cases. 
The Ministry could have laid both the notifications during the 194 th (Winter Session 
2001) of the Rajya Sabha, but they failed to do so. The Committee hopes that they 
would take necessary action and avoid such instances. 
                          
viii.      Ministry of Shipping 
The Committee regrets to note that the Ministry of Shipping has laid five 
notifications during the 195th Session and three out of them were delayed by a period 
ranging from 4-8 months. The Committee expects the Ministry to take necessary and 

corrective action in order to ensure that such delays do not recur and the schedule as 
prescribed by the Committee in the matter of laying of subordinate legislati on is 
followed, strictly.  
  
3.         Besides the above, the Committee also notes with regret the isolated cases of 
delayed laying of notifications by the Ministry of Human Resource Development (sl. 
no. 36 of the Annexure), Ministry of Law, Justice and Company Affairs (sl. no. 249 of 
the Annexure), Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (sl. no. 258 of the 
Annexure) and Ministry of Textiles (sl. no. 258 of the Annexure). The Committee 
would like these  Ministries to take note of the time schedule which is  reproduced 
hereinafter and ensure that the same is complied with meticulously for future. The 
Committee, accordingly, reiterates its observations made in its 135th Report : 
  
 “ The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential 
that in case there is a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the 
concerned Ministry/Department should invariably append a delay 
statement along with the notifications being laid so as t o apprise the 
Parliament of the causes of delay.   The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the intention is that 
through the process of formulation of a delay statement the Ministry is 
able to introspect, identifying b ottlenecks and devising remedial 
measures”.   
  
4.         The Committee impresses again upon all the Ministries/Departments to follow 
the time schedule for laying as prescribed by it in its 131st Report as reproduced below 
:- 
  
“Orders required to be laid  before the House should be laid   (i) if the 
House is not in Session, during the Session immediately following the 
date of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the 
House is in Session, on the date of the publication of the Order, during 
its continuance and in case the time lag between the date of publication 
and the date of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear days, 

before the expiry of the Session immediately following the said 
Session.  All the Ministries/Departments of  Government of India 
should henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of 
the orders issued under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the 
Rajya Sabha.”

2.         The Committee, thereafter, took up for consideration its draft 142nd Report on 
the Statutory Orders laid on the Table of Rajya Sabha during the 195 th Session. The 
Committee noted with serious concern the delay on the part of 
Ministries/Departments in la ying of the various rules/regulations before the 

Parliament. There was a reference to the delay of 17 and 12 years, respectively in the 
laying of the Tobacco Board General Regulations, 1984 and the Tobacco Board 
Recruitment Regulations, 1989 by the Ministr y of Commerce and Industry. The 
Committee took a serious view on the Ministry’s statement that it was not possible 
for them to confirm beyond doubt whether these regulations had been laid before the 
Parliament earlier due to relevant records being not trac eable. The Committee felt 
this to be a sorry state of affairs and desired that such matters alongwith other cases 
where there has been a long delay in the laying of the rules/regulations be taken up 
with the concerned Ministries. The Committee also decided  that these 
Ministries/Departments in whose cases, there has been persistent delay in laying of 
the rules/regulations despite repeated recommendations/observations by it may also 
be identified and the   Secretary incharge of such Ministries/ Departments may  be 
asked to appear before the Committee for clarifications.  
  
3.         During the course of discussion on the draft Report, there was also a mention 
about the delay in framing of the subordinate legislation under various Acts of 
Parliament. A view was expressed that there should be some definite criteria for 
ascertaining whether there has been a delay in framing of the rules/ regulations or 
not. While it was appreciated that the process of framing of subordinate legislations 
was t ime consuming and the time required for the purpose may vary from one 
legislation to another, but, there was a suggestion that the Ministries/Departments 
may also be required to indicate in the memorandum of delegated legislation 
appended to the Bill, whic h gives the areas which are contemplated to be covered 
through subordinate legislation, the approximate time which would be required for 
framing the subordinate legislation and any delay beyond this time limit could be 
pursued by the Committee as a case of  delay. The Committee desired this aspect to 
be examined. The Committee also desired the Secretariat to examine the cases where 
there has been an unusual delay in framing of the rules/regulations for its 
consideration. The draft 142nd Report was, thereafter, adopted.
